name: EEG neurofeedback (Othmer ILF, NeurOptimal, qEEG/LORETA z-score, home and consumer headbands such as Muse/Myndlift)
founders: Siegfried and Susan Othmer (EEG Spectrum/EEG Institute, ILF)
Valdeane W. Brown and Susan Dermit Brown (Zengar Institute, NeurOptimal)
Ariel Garten, Trevor Coleman, Chris Aimone (InteraXon/Muse)
founded_year_range: 1962-1972 for the field (Kamiya alpha training in the early 1960s, Sterman SMR/epilepsy ~1967-72); clinical revival in the 1990s (SSNR 1995); Zengar 1996, NeurOptimal system 2000 (brand name 2008); ILF ~2006 (Othmer et al. 2013: 'over the last 7 years'); InteraXon 2007, Muse released 2014
delivery: home rental device with remote supervision
cost_summary: Clinic: ~US$100-200/session x 20-40 sessions (US$2,000-8,000+), plus a qEEG map (~US$200-600) and initial evaluation (~US$100-400) (market ranges per Myndlift cost article, 2026). NeurOptimal FAQ (2026): US$75-150/session; home rental ~US$600-1,200/month; purchase from ~US$5,995. Muse 2 US$249.99 or Muse S Athena US$474.99, plus Premium app US$49.99/yr. Myndlift is a monthly subscription (Muse headband plus remote clinician); own price not published; guided at-home NF typically US$150-700/month; FSA/HSA via Truemed letter of medical necessity.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
limbic system impairment / amygdala threat conditioning
mechanism_summary: The shared premise is that symptoms reflect dysregulated brain oscillations, arousal or network dynamics. Real-time EEG feedback trains the brain by operant conditioning toward more regulated patterns, which then persist through plasticity. Classic and Othmer ILF models map conditions onto over- or under-arousal and instability: SMR/alpha up-training and theta/high-beta inhibit for pain and sleep, alpha-theta for trauma. qEEG/LORETA models normalise z-score deviations from a database. Research protocols for fibromyalgia target amygdala/limbic or pgACC-S1 networks (central sensitisation). NeurOptimal rejects diagnosis-specific protocols: it interrupts music at EEG 'turbulence' so the brain 'self-organises'. Muse trains meditation attention. Critics attribute much of the benefit to placebo and psychosocial factors.
techniques: qEEG brain map assessment vs normative database
SMR (12-15 Hz) up-training with theta/high-beta inhibit
infra-low frequency (ILF) training titrated to symptom report
home rental systems with remote supervision
consumer EEG meditation feedback (Muse) and gamified app training (Myndlift)
mainstream_notes: Used in some academic, VA and integrative pain/psychiatry settings and in a large private-practice ecosystem with its own certification (ISNR, AAPB, BCIA). Not a first-line recommendation in pain, fibromyalgia or ADHD guidelines; ADHD enthusiasm was undercut by blinded trials. Clinical EEG biofeedback devices are FDA Class II (21 CFR 882.5050, 510(k)-exempt) for relaxation; BCIA offers Board Certified in Neurofeedback (BCN); an earlier AAP-circulated PracticeWise chart rated biofeedback Level 1 for ADHD, but the 2020 edition has no ADHD row; NeurOptimal and Muse market as wellness, not treatment.
insurance_notes: Billed under biofeedback (CPT 90901) or psychophysiological therapy (90875/90876) codes; coverage is inconsistent. Aetna CPB 0132 covers biofeedback for migraine/tension headache only with EMG, thermal or skin modalities ('EEG biofeedback not covered'). It lists biofeedback for ADHD, anxiety, depression, insomnia, PTSD and chronic pain including fibromyalgia as experimental, and amygdala-related EEG NF for PTSD as experimental. Mostly cash pay; consumer/home programs may be FSA/HSA-eligible (e.g., Myndlift via Truemed letter of medical necessity).

key_trials.citation: Kayiran S et al. 2010, Appl Psychophysiol Biofeedback 35:293-302
key_trials.design: Rater-blind RCT, SMR NF (20 sessions over 4 weeks) vs escitalopram 8 weeks, fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Both groups improved; NF superior on pain, psychological symptoms and QoL (p<.05). EEG band amplitudes unchanged (only theta/SMR ratio fell)

key_trials.citation: Wu YL et al. 2021, Pain Manag Nurs 22:755-763
key_trials.design: RCT, 8-week SMR/alpha NF (n=60) vs telephone support (n=20), fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Improved pain severity, pain interference, FIQR, sleep latency and PVT errors vs control

key_trials.citation: Or-Borichev A et al. 2025, BMC Med 23:304
key_trials.design: Double-blind RCT: amygdala-EFP NF (21) vs sham NF (13) vs TAU (13), 10 sessions, fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Real NF reduced symptom severity (eta-p2=.27) and FIQ (eta-p2=.33) short and long term; sham reduced only long-term pain

key_trials.design: Placebo-controlled RCT of amygdala-EFP NF (25 real, 9 sham), fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Objective sleep improved only with real NF; no specific self-report effect at end of training; delayed pain benefit at follow-up, predicted by sleep and affect changes

key_trials.citation: Anderson L et al. 2025, Sci Rep 15:209
key_trials.design: Placebo-controlled feasibility RCT, pgACC-S1 alpha effective-connectivity NF (12 sessions), fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Safe and feasible; pain and function improvements comparable in active and placebo arms

key_trials.citation: Patel K et al. 2020, Eur J Pain 24:1440-1457
key_trials.design: Systematic review/meta-analysis, 21 studies (EEG and fMRI NF), chronic pain
key_trials.finding: Pooled RCT d=-0.76 (95% CI -1.31 to -0.20), I2=73%; mostly low-quality evidence

key_trials.citation: Hesam-Shariati N et al. 2022, Eur J Neurol 29:921-936
key_trials.design: Systematic review/meta-analysis, 10 RCTs + 13 non-randomised, chronic pain
key_trials.finding: Clinically meaningful short-term pain reduction, low GRADE certainty (moderate after excluding high risk-of-bias studies)

key_trials.citation: Arina GA et al. 2022, Front Hum Neurosci 16:891323
key_trials.design: Randomised-order sham-controlled crossover, 10 ILF vs 10 sham sessions plus psychoeducation/support, tension-type headache
key_trials.finding: Real but not sham sessions reduced modelled headache probability

key_trials.citation: van der Kolk BA et al. 2016, PLoS One 11:e0166752
key_trials.design: RCT vs waitlist, T4-P4 NF 24 sessions, chronic PTSD
key_trials.finding: Post-treatment PTSD diagnosis 27% NF vs 68% waitlist; no sham control

key_trials.citation: Askovic M et al. 2023, Eur J Psychotraumatol 14:2257435
key_trials.design: Systematic review (10 controlled studies), meta-analysis of 7 RCTs, PTSD
key_trials.finding: SMD -1.76 (95% CI -2.69 to -0.83) for PTSD symptoms; small heterogeneous studies; first author directs an NF institute

key_trials.design: Double-blind sham-controlled RCT, theta/beta NF, ADHD children
key_trials.finding: No specific NF effect vs sham at end of treatment (d=0.01) or at 13 months

key_trials.design: 25-month follow-up of the double-blind sham-controlled RCT, ADHD children
key_trials.finding: No difference vs control; large within-group gains attributed to non-specific effects

key_trials.citation: Schonenberg M et al. 2017, Lancet Psychiatry 4:673-684
key_trials.design: Triple-blind RCT: NF vs sham vs metacognitive group therapy, adult ADHD
key_trials.finding: All groups improved; NF not superior to sham or group therapy
Effects only with least-blinded raters; null with probably-blinded raters and sham/active controls

controversy: Sham neurofeedback often matches real neurofeedback ('neuroplacebo'; Thibault & Raz 2017), and the best blinded ADHD trials (including a 25-month follow-up) found no specific effect. Pain and fibromyalgia trials are small and mostly unblinded, with heterogeneous protocols. In one RCT EEG band amplitudes did not change despite clinical gains, and pooled evidence is low-certainty. qEEG brain maps are criticised as over-sold diagnostics. NeurOptimal claims 'millions of sessions... no reported side effects' under a wellness disclaimer, and no RCTs of it were found. Some reviews and trials involve NF practitioners or institute directors. Courses are expensive and practitioner quality varies. Side effects (headache, nausea, drowsiness, insomnia, agitation) are under-studied. No trials exist in ME/CFS, POTS, MCS, IBS or long COVID.

popularity.reach_estimate: ~1-3 million people cumulatively. Basis: Muse 500k+ plus Myndlift 41k+ plus NeurOptimal 'millions of sessions' (~30 sessions/person, implying ~10^5 people) plus 3+ decades of clinic NF in thousands of practices worldwide (likely ~10^5-10^6 clients) plus the 1970s biofeedback wave.
popularity.method_notes: Google Trends (HTTP 429) and reddit.com (HTTP 403) block automated access, so 2026 figures were not obtained; a third-party Reddit count (subredditstats.com, Dec 2023) and PubMed yearly counts are used instead. The trajectory is anchored on documented milestones: the late-1960s/70s alpha-biofeedback fad and its 1980s decline; the 1990s clinical revival (SSNR 1995, Othmer network); Zengar 1996/NeurOptimal 2000; LORETA/z-score growth around 2005-10; Muse launch 2014 and The Body Keeps the Score (2014); the remote/home boom during COVID (Myndlift, Muse user claims); and a steady rise in pain meta-analyses and limbic-NF trials 2019-2025. Negative ADHD trials (2016-2023) dampened medical credibility but not consumer uptake. Company user and session counts were re-checked on the sites in Oct 2026 and are self-reports.
